name: steve_update
description: Tell Steve (and the user) what you are doing now and your current plan. Call it when you start, and whenever the plan or your current step changes.

now.description: one short sentence, in the user's language

name: steve_ask
description: Ask the user a question you cannot answer yourself. Prefer concrete options. Do not ask in plain text; use this tool, then end your turn.

options.description: 2–4 choices; the user may also answer freely

recommended.description: the option you would pick (one of options)

why.description: one sentence: why you recommend it

name: steve_request_approval
description: Ask the user to approve an action with outside effects before doing it: deploying or releasing, sending a message or email, spending money, deleting data, pushing to a shared branch.

detail.description: exactly what will happen, so the user can decide

name: steve_deliver
description: Deliver the finished work for the user's acceptance. Include what you produced and the checks you ran. Then end your turn.

summary.description: what was done and how it was verified, in the user's language

kind.description: e.g. 分支, 提交, PR, 文件, 文档

role.description: result (default): what the goal asked for. record: evidence of the work, not the result itself, such as self-check screenshots, logs, test reports or intermediate files; the item shows them in its work record instead of its outputs

outputs.description: the final deliverables; a newer delivery replaces the outputs of an earlier one, so list everything that is still current

operated.description: true when you actually used the running thing yourself (opened the page and clicked through, ran the upgrade, called the live API), not a build or a test; name the check with what you saw

checks.description: build, tests, manual checks you actually ran

unfinished.description: plan steps (exact text) you deliberately left open; every other step must already be done, or the delivery is refused

name: steve_publish
description: Ask the user to release a new version of Steve from your branch, after the item was accepted. Steve rebases the branch onto main (a conflict comes back to you), fast-forwards main to it, waits for other running work to finish, builds, restarts itself and rolls back if the health check fails. Then end your turn; the result arrives later.

branch.description: the git branch to release, e.g. steve/st-12

summary.description: what changes for the user, in Chinese
